svg.text: C-D SKIN — soft vessels squeezed from outside and turned inside out
The machine never touches the food: paddles and rollers work through a silicone bag; to empty and wash it, the bag is everted.
bag: Ø170 × 180 deep, 3 L, 1.5 mm platinum silicone, steel rim
walker: 2 paddles 120 × 120, stroke 40, 4 Hz, 300 N
patty die Ø70 + wire: pucks of 100 g ±10 %
eversion 10–30 N, residue < 1 % [?] (bowl 5–15 %)
8 actuators · envelope ≈ 700 × 600 × 900
ONE BAG, FIVE JOBS (section)
pan on hob

g.text: bag hangs by its rim on the scale
turn mouth-down, die ring on rim

svg.text: FOLDER ("Mappe"): dough rolled between two sheets
peel bar lifts the top sheet back at 150°
roller on the top sheet,
gap stepped down
spine / hinge
sheets 330 × 180 × 1.5 silicone
Peel bar lifts the top sheet at 150°; the folder is then inverted
over the tray and the second sheet peeled: a 2 mm sheet is
transferred without ever being lifted. No flour, nothing sticks.
Same folder: Schnitzel flattened by a 1.5 kN platen to 5 mm and
breaded by closing and shaking — the platen never touches meat.
weak point: a skin cannot cut, cook or whip; silicone takes up
odours (colour-coded sets, bake-out, leak test at 50 mbar)

g.text: 1/7 A box is inverted into a silicone bag that hangs by its steel rim on the scale.
2/7 Walker: two paddles squeeze the bag in turn — the mass is kneaded through the skin.
3/7 A patty die ring goes on the rim; the bag is turned mouth-down over the pan (sticky mass stays put).
4/7 Two rollers close on the bag and travel to the rim: a log leaves the die, a wire cuts 100 g pucks.
5/7 A mandrel pushes the floor through the rim: the bag turns inside out and peels off the rest.
6/7 Washed inside out on the turning mandrel: a smooth dome with no corner, sprayed by four jets.
7/7 Mandrel retracts with the rim held: right side out, dried by hot air through the mandrel.
